en: Unlike most substances, solid water ice is less dense than its liquid form, which is why ice cubes float.
When iron rusts, it chemically bonds with oxygen from the air, creating a completely new, heavier substance called iron oxide.
A mixture of cornstarch and water is a non-Newtonian fluid that acts like a liquid when poured but solid when punched.
Helium gas is significantly less dense than the surrounding air, providing the upward buoyant force that makes party balloons float.
Solid dry ice undergoes sublimation, transforming directly into cold carbon dioxide gas without ever melting into a liquid first.
Mixing baking soda and vinegar triggers a chemical reaction that rapidly produces carbon dioxide gas, creating the fizzing bubbles you see.
The metal gallium melts at just under thirty degrees Celsius, meaning a solid piece will literally melt into a puddle in your warm hand.
Oil and water form a heterogeneous mixture because their molecules naturally repel each other, preventing them from dissolving into a uniform solution.
The sun is composed mostly of plasma, a superheated fourth state of matter where intense heat strips electrons away from atoms.
Liquid sweat absorbs thermal energy from your skin to evaporate into a gas, which is the physical process that cools your body.
Sugar dissolves much faster in hot tea than in iced tea because higher temperatures give water molecules more kinetic energy to break sugar crystals apart.
Liquid nitrogen is incredibly cold at minus one hundred ninety-six degrees Celsius, instantly freezing a wet sponge rock-hard upon contact.
